'''Jan van Houwelingen''' (8 December 1937 – 17 March 2013) was a Dutch politician of the defunct [[Anti-Revolutionary Party]] (ARP) later the [[Christian Democratic Appeal]] (CDA) party and chemist.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://nos.nl/artikel/485617-van-houwelingen-cda-overleden.html |title=Van Houwelingen (CDA) overleden - NOS Nieuws |publisher=Nos.nl |date= 17 March 2013|accessdate=2013-03-22}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.online-familieberichten.nl/pers/1087420/Jan-van-Houwelingen-1937-2013 |title=Death notice – Trouw, 19 March 2013 |publisher=Trouw |date= |accessdate=2024-05-27}}</ref>

Van Houwelingen applied at the [[Utrecht University]] in June 1962 [[Major (academic)|majoring]] in [[Chemistry]] and obtaining a [[Bachelor of Science]] degree in July 1964. Van Houwelingen served in the [[Royal Netherlands Army]] as a [[second lieutenant]] from November 1964 until November 1966. Van Houwelingen worked as a chemist and researcher in the [[private sector]] from November 1962 until March 1973. Van Houwelingen served on the [[Municipal council (Netherlands)|Municipal Council]] of [[Leerdam]] from April 1968 until June 1974 and served on the [[States-provincial|Provincial-Council]] of [[Utrecht (province)|Utrecht]] from June 1970 until June 1974. Van Houwelingen became a [[House of Representatives (Netherlands)|Member of the House of Representatives]] after the resignation of [[Barend Biesheuvel]], taking office on 7 March 1973. After the [[1977 Dutch general election|election of 1977]] the Christian Democratic Appeal and the [[People's Party for Freedom and Democracy]] (VVD) formed the [[First Van Agt cabinet|Cabinet Van Agt-Wiegel]], Van Houwelingen and several Christian Democratic Appeal Members of the House of Representatives were critical on the coalition agreement and formed an informal [[caucus]] in their own [[parliamentary group]] called the ''{{Ill|CDA-loyalists|nl|CDA-loyalistenl}}'' that followed the [[First Van Agt cabinet|cabinet]] critically throughout the entire period. After the [[1981 Dutch general election|election of 1981]] Van Houwelingen was appointed as [[List of Ministers of Defence of the Netherlands#List of State Secretaries for Defence|State Secretary for Defence]] in the [[Second Van Agt cabinet|Cabinet Van Agt II]], taking office on 14 September 1981. The Cabinet Van Agt II fell just seven months into its term on 12 May 1982 and continued to serve in a [[Demissionary cabinet|demissionary]] capacity until it was replaced by the [[Caretaker government|caretaker]] [[Third Van Agt cabinet|Cabinet Van Agt III]] with Van Houwelingen continuing as State Secretary for Defence, taking office on 29 May 1982. After the [[1982 Dutch general election|election of 1982]] Van Houwelingen returned as a Member of the House of Representatives, taking office on 16 September 1982. Following the [[September–November 1982 Dutch cabinet formation|cabinet formation of 1982]] Van Houwelingen continued as State Secretary for Defence in the [[First Lubbers cabinet|Cabinet Lubbers I]], taking office on 4 November 1982. After the [[1986 Dutch general election|election of 1986]] Van Houwelingen again returned as a Member of the House of Representatives, taking office on 3 June 1986. Following the [[1986 Dutch cabinet formation|cabinet formation of 1986]] Van Houwelingen remained as State Secretary for Defence in the [[Second Lubbers cabinet|Cabinet Lubbers II]], taking office on 14 July 1986. After the [[1989 Dutch general election|election of 1989]] Van Houwelingen once again returned as a Member of the House of Representatives, taking office on 14 September 1989. Following the [[1989 Dutch cabinet formation|cabinet formation of 1989]] Van Houwelingen was not giving a cabinet post in the new [[Third Lubbers cabinet|cabinet]], the Cabinet Lubbers II was replaced by the [[Third Lubbers cabinet|Cabinet Lubbers III]] on 7 November 1989 and he continued to serve in the House of Representatives as a [[frontbencher]] chairing several [[Parliamentary committee of the Dutch parliament]]. In December 1993 Van Houwelingen announced that he wouldn't not stand for the [[1994 Dutch general election|election of 1994]] and continued to serve until the end of the parliamentary term on 17 May 1994. In May 1994 Van Houwelingen was nominated as [[Haarlemmermeer|Mayor of Haarlemmermeer]], serving from 1 June 1994 until 1 January 2003.
